newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria shares sag, shrug off new finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Austria shares sag, shrug off new finance minister.

text.p: Austrian shares lost ground on Friday amid weak international leads, with news of a new finance minister failing to inspire the market.
Vienna City finance chief Rudolf Edlinger will take over the finance ministry from chancellor-designate Viktor Klima.
"I didn't even register the announcement," said one trader in reference to the news that broke some two hours before the market closed.
Analysts said markets had hoped for an expert outsider rather than a little-known career politician to tackle budget problems in the run-up to Europe's single currency.
The ATX index fell 7.90 points, or 0.67 percent, to 1,178.96, with 14 shares lower and seven higher.
But traders said the market proved relatively resilient in the face of weak international leads and see market recovering next week.
The leading decliner was Creditanstalt ordinaries, down 2.63 percent at 667 schillings, while EA-Generali ordinaries were the top performer, adding on 1.88 percent to 3,250.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index fell 1.19 points, or 0.27 percent, to 440.64.
The February ATX future lost seven points to 1,185 on turnover of 462 contracts.
